clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old woman developed high fever, worsening kidney function, frequent sinus pauses (~5s), paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, palpitations, and discomfort after her second course of pembrolizumab monotherapy. Initial workup revealed elevated cardiac biomarkers (troponin I 0.032 ng/mL, NT-proBNP 1,724 pg/mL). An echocardiogram showed preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (60-65%) with no asynergy, pericardial effusion, or valvular disease. Coronary angiography confirmed no coronary artery stenosis. An endomyocardial biopsy of the right ventricular septum revealed infiltration by CD3-positive lymphocytes and CD163-positive macrophages adjacent to degenerated/necrotic myocytes, with localized PD-L1 immunopositivity and positive tenascin-C immunostaining, confirming myocarditis. Pulse steroid therapy (1g methylprednisolone for 3 days, followed by 1mg/kg prednisolone) was initiated. This led to an increase in eGFR, a decrease in troponin I and NT-proBNP levels, and a reduction in the frequency of sinus pauses. The sick sinus syndrome resolved after steroid therapy, allowing for removal of the temporary pacemaker. The clinical course and biopsy findings supported the conclusion of ICI-induced myocarditis.
